name: application-pdf-page-thumbnails
title: PDF Page Thumbnails
description: A scrollable rail of document page thumbnails with an active-page highlight, paired with a main viewer pane showing the selected page.
useWhen: Viewing a multi-page document (PDF, slide deck, scanned pages) where jumping directly to a page beats sequential scrolling.
Users benefit from a persistent visual map of the whole document alongside the page they're currently reading.
avoidWhen: The document is a single page or very short — the thumbnail rail adds overhead without navigational benefit.
You need general file browsing across many separate documents — a `File Tree` or list view fits that better than page-level thumbnails.
responsiveBehavior: The thumbnail rail keeps a fixed width and scrolls its own y-axis independently of the main viewer pane; on narrow viewports collapse the rail into a toggleable drawer instead of shrinking it further.
accessibility: The rail is wrapped in a <nav aria-label="Page thumbnails"> landmark distinct from the main viewer content.
Each thumbnail button carries aria-current="true" on the active page, not solely a border/color change.
Page numbers are rendered as visible text below each thumbnail and restated in the viewer pane ("Page 1 of 5"), not conveyed by position alone.

variants.title: Thumbnail rail with viewer
variants.description: A five-page thumbnail rail (page 1 active, ring-highlighted) beside a main viewer pane showing the selected page and a 'Page 1 of 5' caption.
accessibility: The active thumbnail carries aria-current="true" and a page-number label.

variants.title: Thumbnail rail with viewer (Dark)
variants.description: PDF page thumbnail rail and viewer adapted for dark surfaces.
accessibility: The active-thumbnail border and page-number text meet WCAG AA contrast against the dark rail background.
